topics.title: A one-act comic play: how plays work

learn.hook: A man comes to propose marriage, but ends up fighting about a meadow and a dog. Only on stage!
points: 'The Proposal' by Anton Chekhov is a one-act comic play: Lomov visits his neighbour Chubukov to propose to his daughter Natalya.
Before he can propose, Lomov and Natalya quarrel about the Oxen Meadows, and later about whose dog is better. They get engaged, but keep quarrelling.
A one-act play is short, has one act, few characters and usually one setting.
A play is told through dialogue; stage directions (often in brackets or italics) tell actors how to move and speak.
A farce is a comedy built on exaggerated characters and silly situations.

example.q: Scene: RAHUL (nervously): Uncle, I have come to ask... to ask... / MR VERMA (smiling): Speak up, beta! / RAHUL (clutching his chest): My heart is pounding! What do the words in brackets do?
steps: '(nervously)', '(smiling)', '(clutching his chest)' are not spoken aloud.
They tell the actor how to speak or what to do.
So they are stage directions.
example.answer: They are stage directions: they show how the characters speak and act.

learn.reallife: School annual-day plays, street plays (nukkad natak) and TV sitcoms all use dialogue and stage directions.

topics.title: Chekhov and comic characters: describing traits

learn.hook: A man who claims his heart is pounding and his leg is numb, every few minutes! Chekhov makes it hilarious.
points: Anton Chekhov (1860-1904) was a Russian writer of plays and short stories, and also a doctor.
In 'The Proposal', Lomov keeps complaining about his health: palpitations, a numb leg. He worries too much about illness.
The humour comes from exaggeration and irony: people meant to be planning a marriage quarrel over trifles.
Character-trait words: quarrelsome (likes to argue), hypochondriac (worries too much about health), irritable (easily annoyed), impulsive (acts without thinking).
Many adjectives come from nouns with suffixes: quarrel → quarrelsome, nerve → nervous, humour → humorous, anger → angry.

example.q: In the play, Lomov complains of palpitations and a numb foot every time Natalya disagrees with him about a small matter. What trait does this show, and why is it funny?
steps: He reacts to a small argument as if he is seriously ill.
That shows he worries too much about his health: a hypochondriac.
The gap between the tiny cause and his huge reaction is exaggeration, which makes us laugh.
example.answer: He is a hypochondriac; his huge reaction to a small quarrel is comic exaggeration.

learn.reallife: Comedians often exaggerate everyday habits, such as an uncle who checks the gas knob ten times before leaving.
